chains.trait: Hyperthrophic cardiac ventricles with high oxygen affinity
links: Low-gravity moon (F5) allows heavier brains without wing penalty
High O2 partial pressure (F7) maximizes hemoglobin binding saturation
Dual-aerobic hearts sustain flight and cognition simultaneously
Leap upward with height advantage, -20% defense next turn

skill.effect: The creature launches itself high into the sky, gaining a commanding view of the battlefield. While soaring above, its exposed form leaves it strongly vulnerable to nearby strikes.

chains.weakness: Cardiac strain from prolonged flight; ends turn with exhaustion

journal.en: They fly not by grace, but by cardiovascular desperation.

plausibility.summary: Low g (F5) lightens weight-bearing but not aerodynamic power demand; hypertrophic heart is the cost of dual flight + large brain—cap ‘Aero-Thrust’ leaps and tie post-flight exhaustion to lore lifespan (~23 y) and endemic cardiomyopathy rather than unlimited sorties.
fixes: Low g (F5) lightens weight-bearing but not aerodynamic power demand; hypertrophic heart is the cost of dual flight + large brain—cap ‘Aero-Thrust’ leaps and tie post-flight exhaustion to lore lifespan (~23 y) and endemic cardiomyopathy rather than unlimited sorties.

analogues.organism: Flying fox (*Pteropus*) large heart for powered flight; hummingbird extreme cardiac output; bar-headed goose high-O2 hemoglobin affinity
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Hollow trabeculated long bones filled with air sacs
links: Low-g environment (F5) favors ventral feeding and aerial lifestyle
Stable climate (F2) allows prolonged flight without thermal stress
Hollow trabeculated bones reduce structural mass
Reduce incoming kinetic damage by 20% when airborne

skill.effect: Its hollow, air-filled bones allow it to glide effortlessly through the sky. When struck while airborne, the creature's lightweight frame absorbs the impact with remarkable resilience.

chains.weakness: Bones fracture easily if caught in high-wind shear zones

journal.en: Their skeletons are hollow vessels, carrying weightless dreams across a weightless sky.

plausibility.summary: In 0.2 g, pneumatic bones can be extreme but brittle on hard landing—keep F9 wind-shear fracture weakness; pneumatization should invade postcranial skeleton but preserve cortical shell at joint loads (pterosaur/bird pattern).
fixes: In 0.2 g, pneumatic bones can be extreme but brittle on hard landing—keep F9 wind-shear fracture weakness; pneumatization should invade postcranial skeleton but preserve cortical shell at joint loads (pterosaur/bird pattern).

analogues.organism: Bird pneumatic skeleton and air-sac system; pterosaur hollow humeri
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Both exploit low-g/aerial niches; Striders rely on passive buoyancy and heat-dumping flaps, Pterosapiens evolve active flight with hollow bones and hyperthrophic hearts.
